$comment: The properties every mod of a given `kind` carries, merged into each mod's own settings by `schema/build.mjs`. Declared once here so the ninth HUD widget cannot invent its own spelling of `scale`, and so a property added to the set reaches every HUD mod at once instead of being retrofitted into twenty settings pages. `{noun}` in a description is replaced with the mod's own `noun`.

hud.$comment:
Shared by every `kind: hud` mod — the eight that own a draggable HUD item.

The first three are the set VOID already had. The four after them are the HUD chrome block, and they exist because a HUD readout is drawn over *arbitrary game pixels*: a chip that is legible on a stone wall can be unreadable on snow or on a nether ceiling, and until now the only answers a player had were `scale` and `opacity`, neither of which is about contrast.

What this block is deliberately NOT: Lunar gives essentially every HUD mod a background colour, a border colour and per-element text colours. `design/quiet-cell-system.md` §1 puts exactly that on the far side of its line — 'a chip background, border or label colour per mod' is named there as what stays out, because colour in this system encodes a value or a state and is never a preference. So every property here is *structural*: on/off, or a step on a system-owned token scale. The player chooses whether a chip has a ground, never what colour that ground is. §1's own list of what customisation legitimately is — 'position, anchor and offset, scale, opacity, density, what is shown, format' — is the shape of this block, and `padding` is `density` under its own name.

background.description: Ground drawn behind {noun}, as a step on the system's own scale rather than a colour. `none` is the vanilla treatment and the default — the readout sits on the game. `subtle` is the card ground at low alpha, which is enough to hold a chip together over a busy texture; `solid` is the opaque card ground, for a player who wants the HUD to read as a panel. A step rather than a hex value because a per-mod background colour is what §1 names as the far side of the line.

border.description: Whether a hairline is drawn around {noun}, at the system's own `--border-panel` alpha. Boolean rather than a colour or a width for the same reason as `background`: the edge either separates the chip from the game or it does not, and the one useful answer is already a token.

text_shadow.description: Whether glyphs in {noun} carry the vanilla 1px drop shadow. This is the single most load-bearing legibility control on the HUD — it is what makes white text survive a snow biome — and it is on by default because that is what Minecraft itself does and what every player has read text against for a decade.

padding.description: Density of {noun} — the inset between its content and its edge, as one of three steps. `density` is named in §1 as legitimate customisation, and it is what a player actually means by 'make the HUD smaller' when `scale` has already made the text too small to read.

gameplay.$comment: Shared by every `kind: gameplay` mod. There is exactly one: a gameplay mod mutates a client-side option and draws nothing of its own, so it has no chrome, no placement and no size — `crosshair` and `hitboxes` carry their own geometry because it is the geometry of a *world* mark, not of a HUD item.
